clue.text: Client must give her a hand to do her job

definitions.text: Client must give her a hand to do her job

parts.words: Client must give her a hand to do her job
parts.note: giving a hand reads as helping, but here the customer literally offers a hand so its nails can be tended

explanation.surface: A worker relies on her clients pitching in before she can get anything done.
explanation.definitionFit: A nail technician works on a customer's hands, so the hand must be held out to her.

clue.text: Spoil island

definitions.meaning: to spoil something is to mess it up
A small island of the Inner Hebrides, off the west coast of Scotland

explanation.walkthrough: Muck is one of the Small Isles in the Scottish Inner Hebrides.
explanation.definitionFit: Muck up means ruin; Muck is also a Hebridean island's name.

clue.text: Retreat without permission?

parts.note: without means having none, as in a word of refusal
an OK is approval or permission

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether withdrawing without leave is allowed.
explanation.definitionFit: A retreat is a secluded corner or hideaway, a quiet recess to withdraw into.

clue.text: Info prudently gathered before advancing

parts.note: advancing reads as moving forward, but here it means lending money, and the cautious lender checks the borrower first

explanation.surface: A careful scout collects intelligence before an army moves forward.
explanation.definitionFit: Lenders assess a borrower's financial reliability before advancing a loan.

clue.text: Poet starts off rhyming in lines and finishes in blank verse

indicators.note: starts off asks for the opening letter of each of the next three words
finishes in asks for the closing letter of each of the two following words

explanation.surface: A versifier begins with rhyme and ends up writing unrhymed lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Rainer Maria Rilke was the Austrian lyric poet of the Duino Elegies.

clue.text: See us act stupidly with dope, like this?

definitions.text: See us act stupidly with dope, like this?

indicators.note: acting stupidly suggests confusion, so the letters are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Watch us behave like fools after taking drugs: is this what we become?
explanation.walkthrough: 'stupidly' rearranges US ACT and DOPE; the whole clue then describes someone dazed by drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone dazed or stupefied by drugs is described as out of it, vacant.

clue.text: A part of the garden where you'll find retired people

parts.note: a flower bed is a part of a garden

explanation.surface: A garden spot where pensioners gather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired' suggests pensioners, but it means gone to bed for the night.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who have retired for the night are lying in bed, so that is where they are found.

clue.text: Ultimate criterion — for example What is Pyramus?

definitions.meaning: the deciding factor or essential point in the end
in A Midsummer Night's Dream the weaver Bottom plays Pyramus, so Pyramus is the part he speaks

explanation.surface: A drama student is asked to define a final test using a Shakespearean example.
explanation.definitionFit: The deciding factor is the last figure on a balance sheet; Pyramus is the role Bottom speaks.

clue.text: Racehorse found in county

parts.note: the Derby is a famous English flat race
a shire is a breed of heavy draught horse

explanation.surface: A thoroughbred is discovered in a rural district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Racehorse' splits into race (the Derby, run at Epsom) and horse (a shire). DERBYSHIRE is an English county in the Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Derbyshire is one of the shires of England's East Midlands.

clue.text: Class on the other side of road intersection

parts.note: CL is a standard abbreviation for class
overleaf means on the other side of the page

explanation.surface: A school group stands across the street from a junction.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloverleaf is a motorway junction whose looped slip roads resemble a four-leafed plant.

clue.text: Top player, one of fifty representing states

definitions.meaning: a leading performer or celebrity in a team or cast
the US flag has fifty five-pointed emblems, one for each state

explanation.definitionFit: A leading performer is the headline name; the American flag carries one such emblem per state.

clue.text: Journalists writing article supporting crew, say

indicators.note: in a down answer a piece that supports another sits beneath it

parts.note: a four is a rowing crew of four oarsmen
the is the definite article
to state is to say

explanation.surface: Reporters write a feature in support of a boat's crew.
explanation.definitionFit: The press is traditionally called the estate ranking after clergy, nobles and commons.

clue.text: Fiscal policy that could make Co. money?

parts.note: read the answer as an instruction: a jumble of the letters of the second word gives Co. plus money

explanation.surface: A government strategy aimed at making companies profitable.
explanation.definitionFit: An economic system blending private enterprise with state ownership is a policy approach.

clue.text: Stormy spell on the sea between continents

indicators.note: stormy suggests turbulence, so the letters are tossed into a new order

explanation.surface: A rough patch of weather on the water separating Europe and Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dardanelles strait, anciently so named, divides Europe from Asia Minor.

clue.text: They help some viewers to see shows

definitions.text: They help some viewers to see

explanation.definitionFit: Glasses aid eyesight; grand displays are also called by this word.

clue.text: Artificially neat prose?

indicators.note: artificially suggests something made up rather than natural, so the letters are reconstructed

explanation.surface: Is tidy writing produced by artifice?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Artificially' rearranges NEAT PROSE, and the whole clue also describes an invented language.
explanation.definitionFit: Zamenhof's invented international language is a constructed, artificial tongue.

clue.text: Orchid painted by Goya, for one

definitions.meaning: a name for the autumn crocus or an orchid with bare flowering stems
Goya's famous nude, La Maja Desnuda, is an unclothed woman

explanation.definitionFit: A flower with leafless stems bears this name, as does Goya's unclothed Maja.

clue.text: Rover finding river, a sacred one

parts.note: Alph is the sacred river in Coleridge's Kubla Khan

explanation.surface: A wanderer comes upon a holy stream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rover' is Sir Ralph the Rover, the pirate in Southey's ballad The Inchcape Rock.
explanation.definitionFit: Southey's pirate is named Sir Ralph the Rover, so the name fits the title.

clue.text: One caught and landed without staying within the law

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so these letters go round the others

parts.note: lit means landed, as a bird alights
I is the Roman numeral one
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A fisherman lands his catch but stays within the rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside: LIT goes round IC.
explanation.definitionFit: Lawful conduct is permitted, keeping inside legal bounds.

clue.text: Field marshal wrongly put in the nick by king

indicators.note: by means next to, so the king follows
being wrongly put somewhere suggests disorder, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: ER stands for Edwardus Rex, a king's royal cipher

explanation.surface: A senior officer is unjustly jailed by order of the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nick' is British slang for prison; here THE NICK is just fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord Kitchener was a British army field marshal of the First World War era.

clue.text: It colours the view of the outside world of those in the church

definitions.text: It colours the view of the outside world of those in the church

parts.words: It colours the view of the outside world of those in the church
parts.note: colouring a view sounds like biased opinion, but here church windows literally tint what worshippers see

explanation.surface: Religious belief shapes how churchgoers see secular society.
explanation.definitionFit: Coloured window glass in churches tints the light and outlook of the congregation.

clue.text: Pound added to moderate rent

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling
to ease is to moderate or lessen

explanation.surface: A pound is added to make the rent more moderate.
explanation.definitionFit: To lease is to rent property under a contract.

clue.text: Make an impact, introducing new clue

indicators.note: introducing means bringing the letter into the word

parts.note: to hit is to make an impact

explanation.surface: Bring in a fresh clue to make an impression.
explanation.definitionFit: A suggestion or pointer helping a solver is a clue.

clue.text: Detected in bloody error, one's liable to change colour

indicators.note: detected in says the letters can be found inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A mistake spotted in a bloody affair makes someone go pale.
explanation.definitionFit: One who colours fabric or hair changes its colour as a trade.

clue.text: Paints Socialist — nothing odd in that

indicators.note: nothing odd in that means the odd-placed letters of the word are dropped, leaving the even ones

explanation.surface: A left-winger's artwork has nothing strange about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Oil colours are a painter's medium, also used for paintings themselves.

clue.text: Many involved with capital — mostly capital

indicators.note: involved suggests tangled together, so the letters are mixed
mostly means all but the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Lots of people tied up with money, mostly money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims the last letter from capital, giving CAPITA to mix with MANY.
explanation.definitionFit: Panama City is the capital of the Central American country Panama.

clue.text: Cast argued when decision is disputed

definitions.meaning: to cast is to throw or fling
to argue the ... is to dispute a decision already made

explanation.definitionFit: Throwing something is flinging it; 'argue the toss' is the idiom for disputing a ruling.

clue.text: Old craftsman is kind to dog

parts.note: a type is a kind or sort
a setter is a breed of gun dog

explanation.surface: A veteran artisan is gentle with his dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kind' looks like an adjective (gentle) but is the noun sort.
explanation.definitionFit: Compositors arranged metal letters for printing, a craft largely superseded.
